name: Arakas (Greek Peas With Potatoes and Carrots)

ingredients.name: olive oil, plus additional for garnish, divided

instructions.primary_message: Dice the yellow onion. Cut the carrots into 1-inch-thick rounds. Mince the garlic. Cut the yellow potatoes into 1 1/2-inch pieces. Pick the dill fronds from the stems and chop them. Juice the lemon.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 medium yellow onion
3 carrots
1 large clove garlic
2 large yellow potatoes
½ cup fresh dill fronds
½ lemon

instructions.primary_message: In a large heavy-bottomed saucepot, heat 3 tablespoons olive oil over medium-high until shimmering. Add onion and 1 teaspoon kosher salt and cook until onion is softened and translucent, about 7 minutes.

Add carrot, garlic, tomato paste, miso, and 1 tablespoon olive oil, and cook, stirring constantly, until garlic is fragrant, about 1 minute. Add potatoes, diced tomatoes, and remaining 1 teaspoon kosher salt, and stir to combine.

Add just enough water to cover potatoes (about 2 about cups). Cover with the lid and bring to a boil, then remove lid and reduce heat to medium-low to maintain a simmer, and cook until the potatoes are fork-tender, 15 to 20 minutes.

Add peas, dill, and remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil, and stir to combine. Continue cooking on medium heat, uncovered, stirring occasionally, until peas are heated and cooked through, and sauce has thickened and coats the peas and potatoes (it should not be watery or soupy), an additional 5 to 8 minutes.

Add lemon juice, season to taste with salt and pepper, stir to combine, and let sit for about 10 minutes to cool slightly. Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with more olive oil and a side of feta and fresh bread.

description: This classic Greek arakas—peas braised with potatoes, carrots, and tomatoes—is an easy one-pot side dish that’s make-ahead friendly and perfect for spring.
notes:
Optional or for serving: Feta cheese for serving; Crusty bread or pita for serving

Optional substitutions: freshly squeezed lemon juice → apple cider vinegar

Make-ahead and storage: The dish can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 4 days.
author: Sharon Brenner
